name: Billitonnen
description: Billitonnen is a traditional Dutch domino game belonging to the 'Blind Hughie' family. Players draw their tiles but keep them face-down in a row, turning them over one at a time to play. The strong element of luck is tempered by memory—if you can remember the positions of tiles you've seen others fail to play, you gain a significant advantage. Traditionally played as light relief after a session of the more serious Dutch game Nos.

history.origins: Originating in the Netherlands, Billitonnen takes its name from Billiton (Belitung), an Indonesian island formerly part of the Dutch East Indies. It is a lighthearted variant of European line games, prized for its chaotic and social nature.
timeline: 19th Century: Blind domino games become popular in European cafes.
Early 20th Century: Billitonnen establishes itself as the standard Dutch 'wind-down' game.
Present: Still played in traditional Dutch gaming circles and recorded in national heritage archives.
history.cultural: A classic 'after-match' game, meant to be played with drinks and conversation rather than intense competitive focus.
history.evolution: The game follows the 'Blind Hughie' template but introduces the strict 'Leftmost First' rule, which increases the frustration and humor of the game.

setup.dealing: Players draw tiles based on count (2p=7, 3p=7, 4p=6). Tiles are placed in a face-down row in front of each player. No one may look at their tiles.

rules.objective: Be the first player to empty your face-down row by matching tiles to the central line.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Start**: A tile is drawn from the boneyard to start the line. 2. **The Turn**: On your turn, flip over the LEFTMOST face-down tile in your row. 3. **The Match**: If the tile matches either open end of the central line, you must play it. 4. **The Failure**: If the tile does not match, you must turn it face down again in its original position. 5. **Boneyard**: Unused tiles are not drawn; the game relies only on the initial hand.
keyRules: You must always turn the leftmost tile first.
Memory is your only tool: you must remember what tiles were returned face-down.
The game ends when someone goes domino (empties row) or when no one can move (blocked).

strategy.basic: Memory is essential. When you flip a tile that doesn't match, memorize its pip values. When the line ends change later, you'll know if that specific tile can be played.
strategy.intermediate: Opponent Tracking: Watch what your opponents flip and return. If they return a 5-2, and you have control over the line ends, try to make one of the ends a 5 or 2 to force them to play a tile they might not want to.
strategy.advanced: Block Prevention: If you know your leftmost tile matches an end, but playing it would change that end to a value you know your *next* tile cannot match, consider the risk of blocking yourself.
tips: Don't worry about strategy too much—the 'Leftmost' rule makes it highly luck-dependent.
Try to keep the line ends varied to maximize your chances of a match.

variations.name: Blind Hughie
variations.description: The English variant where players may sometimes choose which tile to flip instead of the leftmost.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Blind Hughie is documented as the parent game; no separate engine overrides for it are modeled in this Billitonnen file yet.

scoring.description: The player who empties their hand first wins the round. In a blocked game, the player with the fewest remaining tiles wins.
scoring.winCondition: Emptying the player's row or having the fewest tiles at a block.

synthesis.shortDescription: A charming Dutch blind domino game. Your tiles sit face-down in a row — turn over the leftmost one and hope it matches. If not, flip it back and remember where it is. Memory is your only weapon in this luck-heavy, laugh-filled game.
